title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Family as a Primary Group
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: In sociological terms taught in Social Studies, which of the following best defines a **primary social group**?
options: A massive group where members interact highly formally and impersonally
A small social group whose members share intimate, face-to-face, and enduring relationships
A temporary group of people gathered exclusively for a political campaign rally
A network of people who communicate solely through online internet forums
questions.explain: A **primary social group** is characterized by small size, direct face-to-face interaction, high emotional connection, and long-lasting relationships.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is widely regarded as the most basic, universal, and first primary social group an individual belongs to?
options: The secondary school
The local peer group
The religious institution
The family
questions.explain: The **family** is the foundational unit of society and serves as the very first primary group an individual is born into and socialized by.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which distinct characteristic primarily makes the family a "primary group" rather than a "secondary group"?
options: The relationships are deep, intimate, emotional, and long-lasting
The members share the exact same political party affiliations
The group relies on formal economic contracts and wage payments
The interactions between members are strictly professional and temporary
questions.explain: Unlike secondary groups (e.g., workplaces, large organizations) which are formal and temporary, the family features relationships that are **intimate, deeply emotional, and enduring**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is one of the most vital roles and responsibilities of the family as a primary social group within a larger society?
options: Passing national laws, regulating elections, and maintaining a national army
Judging high-level criminal cases and issuing legal prison sentences
Socializing children, imparting societal values, and providing basic emotional needs
Signing complex international trade treaties on behalf of the nation
questions.explain: The primary role of the family is **socialization**. This includes providing basic care, teaching cultural norms, molding behavior, and meeting the emotional and economic needs of its members.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following is an expected responsibility of the parents within the family as a primary social group?
options: Enacting federal laws for the community
Providing basic needs like food, shelter, and clothing
Arresting criminals in the neighborhood
Paying taxes on behalf of their neighbors
questions.explain: Within the family setup, parents have the fundamental responsibility of providing basic life necessities such as **food, shelter, and clothing** for their children.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is a major role that children are expected to play as members of the family group?
options: Earning the entire family income
Showing respect and obedience to parents and elders
Making final decisions on family relocations
Paying school fees for themselves
questions.explain: Children have specific roles within the family social group, chief among them being **respecting parents, obeying rules, and assisting with household chores**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
